title: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application Exhaustion Flood (LOIC HTTP)
mitre_source: Borisenko et al. (2022), DOI: 10.1109/SYNCHROINFO55067.2022.9840920, Table II
source_note: key_features: expected salience from ATT&CK documentation, not measured on this dataset. observed_features: top-5 mean |SHAP| over the training reference set of the named Layer 1 variant.
description: Adversaries may cause a DoS by exhausting the resources of an endpoint's application layer. LOIC (Low Orbit Ion Cannon) in HTTP mode floods a target with HTTP GET/POST requests from multiple coordinated hosts to exhaust web server threads and connections.

network_indicators.traffic_pattern: Rapid, repeated HTTP GET/POST requests from multiple coordinated source IPs with minimal inter-arrival time between requests.

mitigation.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigation.action: Rate-limit per-IP request rate and deploy a CDN/WAF with DDoS scrubbing.

mitigation.name: Exploit Protection
mitigation.action: Use connection/thread limits and behavioral anomaly detection to identify coordinated request floods.

false_positive_hints: Aggressive web crawlers or misconfigured monitoring tools polling frequently can resemble low-and-fast HTTP flood traffic.
